source_note: Task descriptions and metric interpretation follow the repository registries and module guides.

scope.question: Evaluation of cell-level velocity predictions, gene-level velocity directions and kinetic-parameter recovery.
scope.summary: 20 RNA velocity method configurations across 14 real datasets and three simulated scenarios. The two scEU-seq systems are included among the 14 real datasets.

tasks.label: Cell-level velocity evaluation
tasks.inputs: Method-specific cellular velocities and annotated transitions.
tasks.outputs: Consistency, ICCoh, CBDir, TransCosine and BATC; method-specific velocity fields.

tasks.label: Gene-level velocity evaluation
tasks.inputs: Spliced and unspliced velocity components in each method’s scoring coordinates.
tasks.outputs: Gene-level CBDir; CosSim against known velocities in simulations; phase portraits.

tasks.label: Kinetic-parameter recovery
tasks.inputs: Cell-specific transcription or degradation profiles aligned to fitted reference trajectories.
tasks.outputs: Paired-finite Spearman correlations for α and γ; reference/prediction trajectories.

scope.interpretation: Browse the saved evaluation results by method, dataset and task. Summary statistics follow the gene sets and aggregation rules of the published tables.

ensembles.note: Mean-4 and RowGeometricMedian-4 (GeoMedian-4) aggregate signed transition rows from four fixed methods. These post-hoc cell-level comparators are evaluated separately against the 20 registered configurations.
ensembles.ranking_note: Each variant is ranked separately against the 20 registered configurations for the same dataset and metric. Rank is 1 + the number of configuration scores strictly above the ensemble score; exact ties use competition rank.

protocol.title: Inputs and preprocessing
protocol.text: The common preprocessing uses the top 2,000 highly variable genes where applicable; method-specific filtering and native input requirements are retained. Raw-count, total-expression and upstream-velocity configurations have their own input contracts.

protocol.title: Fixed reference neighbors
protocol.text: Cell evaluation uses stored 30-nearest-neighbor assets built in X_pca with 30 PCs, Euclidean distance and random state 0. Forebrain CBDir uses the shared 30-PC coordinates and full velocity projection; its streamlines display PC1/PC2. Forebrain BATC uses the shared frozen 2D UMAP. Other datasets retain their registered reference projections.

protocol.title: TransCosine and representation
protocol.text: For the primary Cell benchmark, the scVelo velocity graph is recomputed on fixed candidates using reference Ms aligned to common cells and genes and the unchanged method velocity. veloAE retains native latent Ms because its velocity is defined in a learned latent space. Positive graph weights are not row-normalized transition probabilities.

cell.label: Consistency
cell.definition: Cosine agreement between neighboring velocity vectors.
cell.aggregation: Non-self reference neighbors with positive vector norms are averaged per cell, then across cells; cells with no valid neighbors contribute zero.

cell.label: ICCoh
cell.definition: Velocity coherence within the same annotated cluster.
cell.aggregation: Within-cluster neighbor cosines are averaged per cell and cluster, then across clusters with defined scores.

cell.label: CBDir
cell.definition: Velocity alignment with displacement toward target-cluster neighbors along annotated transitions.
cell.aggregation: Source-cell values are averaged within each valid transition, then transitions receive equal weight.

cell.label: TransCosine
cell.definition: Positive velocity-graph support for annotated downstream transitions.
cell.aggregation: Positive graph weights are averaged over target-cluster neighbors, then valid source cells and defined transition edges. Negative graph weights do not contribute.

cell.label: BATC
cell.definition: Velocity alignment with the tangents of reference lineage curves.
cell.aggregation: The best outgoing branch alignment is retained per source cell; the dataset score is cell-weighted over source clusters. The benchmark replaces non-finite branch scores with zero before branch maximization.

gene.label: Gene-level CBDir
gene.definition: Directional agreement between gene velocity and state displacement in the spliced–unspliced phase plane.
gene.aggregation: Fixed reference-30 target neighbors define displacement vectors. Source-cell cosines are averaged per transition; valid transitions receive equal weight. Zero-norm velocity and zero-length displacement contribute zero. Source-cell observations count participation per edge; one cell can contribute to more than one transition.

gene.label: CosSim
gene.definition: Cosine alignment between inferred and analytical ground-truth vectors in the simulated (s,u) phase plane.
gene.aggregation: The mean uses cells for which both vector norms exceed 10⁻⁶. Valid-cell counts for CosSim are unavailable in the compact table; displayed CBDir counts describe participation in the CBDir calculation.

kinetics.label: Spearman correlation
kinetics.definition: Monotonic agreement between predicted and experimentally fitted kinetic profiles.
kinetics.aggregation: Scores use paired finite positions for each gene/parameter/branch. Fewer than two pairs or a constant trajectory yields an undefined score. Finite gene scores are averaged within a branch; organoid branches and then available systems receive equal weight.

interpretation.title: Gene sets and method coverage
interpretation.text: The real Gene benchmark contains 39 MURK and 20 branching dataset–gene pairs across five and two datasets. Nine configurations provide both ds/dt and du/dt for this comparison. Summaries use each method’s available finite gene scores.

interpretation.title: Canonical and selected kinetic scores
interpretation.text: The selected examples comprise 19 RPE1 genes, six secretory-branch genes and eight enterocyte-branch genes. Canonical cross-experiment summaries use all available finite scores in the stored evaluation, rather than these example subsets. The RPE1 turnover-strategy analysis uses a separate set of 250 matched α/γ trajectories.

interpretation.title: Expanded reference analysis
interpretation.text: The expanded sensitivity analysis uses 250 retained RPE1 reference genes and the same 270 retained organoid genes in each branch. Its available-gene and fixed common-valid-gene summaries are separate comparisons. TSvelo organoid α has 37 matched genes per branch: 20 finite scores and 17 constant predictions; none belongs to the 14 organoid example genes.

interpretation.title: Parameter outputs and the labelled comparator
interpretation.text: cellDancer and DeepVelo provide cell-specific α, β and γ; DeepKINET provides β and γ, with γ scored here; TSvelo provides α. Dynamo in the scEU-seq analysis uses newly synthesized RNA, total RNA and labeling time to estimate α. It is a labelled positive control, distinct from Dynamo(RNA_seq).

interpretation.title: Display units and missing values
interpretation.text: α denotes transcription, β splicing and γ degradation. RPE1 curves are independently z-scored using sample SD for display only. Organoid predictions retain the early-50-bin baseline ratio and references retain their saved source scale on a separate axis. Gaps remain gaps. Missing genes, unavailable parameters and undefined correlations are distinguished; non-finite scores are excluded from summaries, without filling them with zero.

interpretation.title: Phase portraits and numerical scores
interpretation.text: Phase portraits retain saved native coordinates. veloVI numerical scores use restored pre-min–max coordinates and corresponding velocity units. The Gene guide describes the transformations.

method_note: Model characteristics describe the retained paper table. “—” means no explicit entry in that table. Gene-level coverage describes the saved benchmark components and may include repository post-processing; it is separate from the model’s native du/dt output.
